method.credentialHandling: Secret captured in process memory and a temporary process environment variable only; neither the URL nor credentials were printed or saved. The temporary environment variable was removed after use.
method.queryScope: PostgreSQL settings, current-role flags and ownership aggregates, and pg_stat_activity aggregate counts only. No private user rows or query text were read.

applicationConnectionSizing.source: backend/app/database.py and backend/Dockerfile; installed SQLAlchemy QueuePool defaults inspected locally

interpretation.drainSnapshot: No other active client backends and no idle-in-transaction connections were observed at the snapshot time. This is a point-in-time observation, not proof of future quiescence or a load test.
interpretation.capacityRisk: At 20 instances, the current one-process SQLAlchemy defaults allow up to 300 app-to-pooler client sockets. Neon transaction pooling multiplexes these onto PostgreSQL backends, so 300 clients do not imply 300 physical connections. Concurrent or long-running database transactions may still queue or saturate the 106 non-reserved PostgreSQL connection slots.
interpretation.providerDefaultsNotLiveVerified: Neon documents transaction pooling and a per-role/database default_pool_size of 0.9 times max_connections. PgBouncer administration settings were not queried, so that documented default is not asserted as the live pool configuration.
interpretation.followUp: Before broader onboarding, measure concurrent database work and choose explicit SQLAlchemy pool and Cloud Run scale limits with headroom for migrations, operators, and other database clients.
pilotLimitations: The runtime role is not a PostgreSQL superuser but owns the database and tables and has broad role flags; least-privilege runtime credentials remain a follow-up.
Neon Free and the previously accepted six-hour recovery-history window remain temporary pilot limitations. This capacity check did not re-verify the plan or recovery window.
interpretation.releaseDisposition: Sanitized pilot capacity and privilege evidence, not an independent release gate or a claim that the accepted temporary pilot limitations block this release.
